input.question: Why do people generally look different in photos than they do in real life?
input.ground_truth: Lens optics in cameras produce perspective distortions that differ from how our eyes see things. Camera lenses contain multiple lenses that are positioned and move relative to each other to produce different levels of zoom and focus. What you can get is something called [lens compression](_URL_0_) which makes objects seem closer together or further apart than they actually are. This is typically one reason why wedding photographers use lenses with a longer focal length, so that features such as a large nose might seem so prominent.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do people generally look different in photos than they do in real life?

Answer:

response.prediction: Okay! Imagine you have a magic window that only shows you a little piece of the world at a time, not the whole thing. That’s kind of like a camera. When you look at someone with your eyes, you see their whole face and how they move, smile, and talk. But when someone takes a picture, the camera only shows a part of them, and it can’t show how they move or smile naturally. Also, the camera can make things look a little funny sometimes, like making noses look bigger or making people look serious even if they’re not. That’s why people can look a little different in pictures than in real life!
